LESSON: SELECTED CROP MANAGEMENT PRACTISES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Food Production Processes
Topic 2.2: Selected Crop Management Practises

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Selected Crop Management Practises. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we carry out management practises in crop production?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain management practises carried out on crops

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SELECTED CROP MANAGEMENT PRACTISES
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Selected Crop Management Practises helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT PLANTS
Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.
Without water and light, most seedlings wilt.

PART 1: Explain management practises carried out on crops

What this means
In this part you learn to explain management practises carried out on crops. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain management practises carried out on crops.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Selected Crop Management Practises” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain management practises carried out on crops. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Selected Crop Management Practises is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.

Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Selected Crop Management Practises” around your school. (skill: explain management practises carried out on crops)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Selected Crop Management Practises to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain management practises carried out on crops.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Selected Crop Management Practises from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Selected Crop Management Practises: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Selected Crop Management Practises?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we carry out management practises in crop production?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Selected Crop Management Practises means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain management practises carried out on crops.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
